title: Repair Webhook Retry Scheduler
objective: Fix the broken webhook delivery retry scheduler in /app/webhooks/scheduler.py. After a failed delivery attempt, the service must compute the next retry timestamp using exponential backoff with deterministic jitter, honor HTTP Retry-After floors when provided, cap delays at max_delay_ms, and dead-letter deliveries once failed_attempt >= max_attempts. The agent may edit only scheduler.py; companion modules (policy.py, jitter.py, time_utils.py) are correct. Done means compute_schedule satisfies the documented contract, behavioral invariants, and passes visible self-check tests plus held-out hidden and behavioral verifier suites.
motivation: Webhook platforms schedule millions of retries daily. A subtly wrong scheduler causes thundering herds (missing jitter), SLA breaches (ignored Retry-After), or infinite retry loops (off-by-one exhaustion). This task mirrors on-call work triaging a production retry engine where multiple independent bugs stack together — exactly the kind of reasoning frontier agents must demonstrate.
difficultyExplanation: The seed scheduler violates six independent timing rules that each look plausible in isolation: dead-letter uses > instead of >=; backoff exponent is off-by-one; jitter is applied additively; Retry-After floors are ignored; max_delay_ms is never enforced; and timestamps truncate to whole seconds. Agents must read instruction.md, treat helper modules as canonical, and implement the full contract — patching one bug still fails held-out cases with unpublished delivery IDs, alternate multipliers, zero jitter, max_attempts=1, and behavioral property tests (backoff progression, jitter bounds, anti-stub). Hidden tests compare against a sealed spec reference and invariants the agent never sees.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11 (bookworm) container with /app as the working tree. Pre-installed: pytest, bash, curl. The app is a small webhook delivery package under /app/webhooks/ containing a broken scheduler.py plus correct helpers for policy parsing, SHA-256 deterministic jitter, and UTC millisecond time arithmetic. No database, no network services, no runtime package installs — the agent reads instruction.md, inspects the modules, and patches scheduler.py in place. Verifier tests live under /tests/ and import the agent's module dynamically from /app.

networkRequirements.justification: Fully offline debugging task; all dependencies baked into the Docker image at build time.

oracleStrategy: solution/solve.sh installs the reference scheduler.py implementing every instruction.md rule via the provided helpers: dead-letter at failed_attempt >= max_attempts; raw_exponential with exponent (failed_attempt - 1) capped before Retry-After; Retry-After as a floor that does not alter the capped audit flag; multiplicative jitter via deterministic_jitter; millisecond timestamps via add_milliseconds and format_instant. The script runs the full visible, hidden edge, and behavioral pytest suites before grading.
verificationStrategy: Three-layer verifier: (1) test_visible.py — 5 documented self-check cases from instruction.md; (2) test_hidden.py — unpublished delivery IDs, cap/Retry-After semantics, validation, compared to sealed spec_reference.py; (3) test_behavior_hidden.py — behavioral properties (exponential backoff progression, jitter bounds, distinct outputs per delivery ID, stress cap, partner Retry-After dominance, dead-letter audit zeroing). invariants.py enforces now+delay_ms==next_attempt_at on every scheduled result. Multi-channel: literals, spec reference, invariants, and properties. Binary scoring.
binarySuccessCondition: All pytest cases in test_visible.py, test_hidden.py, and test_behavior_hidden.py pass when importing compute_schedule from /app/webhooks/scheduler.py.
partialScoreStrategy: Binary scoring only — no partial credit. Keeps grading deterministic and prevents agents from passing audit subsets or visible literals while leaving core timing logic broken.
anticipatedExploits: 1. Hard-coded responses — Prevention: parametrized wh_unseen_* and wh_matrix_* delivery IDs verified against sealed spec_reference.py; distinct delivery IDs must yield distinct delays. 2. Mock/stub implementation — Prevention: behavioral tests verify exponential backoff progression across failures and jitter bounds on every schedule. 3. Timing manipulation — Prevention: invariants.py asserts next_attempt_at equals now_iso advanced by exactly delay_ms with millisecond precision. 4. Partial single-bug fixes — Prevention: six independent rules each have dedicated hidden/behavioral tests. 5. Random jitter — Prevention: exact SHA-256 deterministic jitter factors asserted. 6. Editing helpers — Prevention: agent may only modify scheduler.py; sealed tests import spec reference at grade time. 7. Audit gaming (capped flag) — Prevention: dedicated test confirms capped reflects pre-Retry-After raw exponential only. 8. Constant delay stub — Prevention: test_distinct_delivery_ids_produce_distinct_delays requires >=3 unique delays across four IDs.
